items.body: Max Meyer has not picked up a stringed instrument on stage in about ten years. The singer of the German industrial metal band Devil-M will do it twice in one weekend: he joins Italian dark electronic act Kirlian Camera as guitarist at the Fuchsbau in Chemnitz on 25 and 26 September 2026. Both nights are sold out, and the band will play a different setlist on each. Danse Macabre Records, Devil-M’s label, announced the guest appearance on 31 August. Meyer described the return to guitar as the part that stands out for him: “Nach so langer Zeit wieder mit einem Saiteninstrument auf der Bühne zu stehen, ist definitiv etwas Besonderes. Gleichzeitig ist es eine spannende Herausforderung, bei zwei Konzerten eine Band wie Kirlian Camera zu unterstützen.” In English: standing on stage with a stringed instrument again after so long is definitely something special, and supporting a band like Kirlian Camera across two concerts is an interesting challenge at the same time. He is known first as a vocalist and frontman of Devil-M, but he has worked as a multi-instrumentalist for years and is credited with drums, synths and arrangement on Devil-M records. The arrangement covers the two Chemnitz nights only. The label states that further shows or projects together are not ruled out. Kirlian Camera tour dates for 2026 and 2027 Kirlian Camera keep a single canonical calendar on their own site and warn against buying tickets for shows that do not appear on it. Seven dates are confirmed: 25 September 2026 – Chemnitz, Germany (Fuchsbau, day 1, doors 20:30, show 21:30, sold out) 26 September 2026 – Chemnitz, Germany (Fuchsbau, day 2, doors 20:30, show 21:30, sold out) 3 October 2026 – Parma, Italy (Santa Maria della Pace Church, Colonne28, “Gala in Nero – Lode”, on stage 20:30, total black dress code) 27 November 2026 – Nuremberg, Germany (Der Cult, headliner) 28 November 2026 – Karlsruhe, Germany (Die Stadtmitte, headliner) 28 February 2027 – Bruges, Belgium (De Donkerste Beurs, festival headliner) 16 May 2027 – Leipzig, Germany (Wave-Gotik-Treffen) Thirteen further entries appear on the same calendar as deliberate placeholders, with no country given. The band reveal those to their mailing list before announcing them publicly. Wave-Gotik-Treffen 2027 runs from 14 to 17 May, so the Leipzig date falls on the Sunday of the festival. About Kirlian Camera Angelo Bergamini founded Kirlian Camera in Parma, Italy, in 1979, and the project became the first Italian act signed to Virgin Records. The line-up changed repeatedly through the 1980s and 1990s across a catalogue that moved between synth-pop, dark electronics, martial and neoclassical material. Elena Alice Fossi joined in 2000 as lead singer and composer, and the Bergamini and Fossi pairing has anchored the band ever since. The group have released through Dependent Records for the last three albums: “Hologram Moon” in 2018, “Cold Pills (Scarlet Gate of Toxic Daybreak)” in 2021 and the double album “Radio Signals For The Dying” on 23 February 2024. That last record runs to sixteen tracks and features Julian Assange. Side-Line covered its announcement in Julian Assange featured on new Kirlian Camera LP ‘Radio Signals For The Dying’ out in 2024 and the singles that preceded it, including “Il Tempo Profondo” and “Götter, geht weg!”. Kirlian Camera are not signed to Danse Macabre Records. The label carries the Chemnitz announcement because its own artist is the guest. About Devil-M Devil-M started in Germany in 2009 and mix industrial metal with gothic metal, with Max Meyer on vocals. Their fourth album, “Titanomachie”, came out on Danse Macabre Records in late 2025 on digital, CD and vinyl, and takes its subject from Greek myth; Side-Line covered it in Devil-M return with Greek myth album ‘Titanomachie’. Meyer has been credited across the band’s records for lyrics, arrangement, percussion and synths alongside his vocals, which is the background to the Chemnitz appearance: the guitar is not a new instrument for him, only one he has kept off stage for a decade.

items.body: Six years after two self-released EPs, Ton:Fehler have a label. The German electronic duo released their debut album “Der Charme des Stumpfen” on 28 August 2026, their first record for Danse Macabre Records. The thirteen tracks run 37 minutes and 41 seconds and mix German EBM with techno, with the two members trading vocals across the record. What is on ‘Der Charme des Stumpfen’ Eleven of the thirteen tracks are new songs: “Der Konjunktiv”, “Evolution Rückwärts”, “Kaputt”, “Bliss Point”, “Bibeltreu und Faktenscheu”, “Normkonform”, “Will ich nicht”, “Erklärer”, “Radsport”, “Tanzreflex” and “Fokus”. Two remixes close the album. Zweite Jugend rework “Bliss Point” and Aktion : Fiasko take on “Erklärer”. “Normkonform”, at 3:32, is the longest song on the record. The lyrics are in German throughout and stay with everyday life rather than genre imagery. Danse Macabre Records describes the album as posing critical questions without supplying answers, and names “Normkonform” as the track that pushes the contradictions furthest. Irony and social criticism run through the writing, and the duo keep the tempo on the dancefloor while they do it. Ton:Fehler on Danse Macabre Records Danse Macabre Records is one of the longer-running German dark electronic labels. Bruno Kramm founded it in Bayreuth in 1989 as a cassette imprint, released early records by Das Ich and Goethes Erben, and coined the term Neue Deutsche Todeskunst for that circle. The label now runs its office and studio from Potsdam. Its current roster includes Devil-M, Oberer Totpunkt, System Noire and Wisborg. “Der Charme des Stumpfen” is Ton:Fehler’s first release through the label; their two earlier EPs came out on their own. The album is available on the usual streaming services. It is not on Bandcamp, where the duo still list only their two EPs. About Ton:Fehler Ton:Fehler are an electronic duo split between Bonn and Bad Salzuflen in Germany, made up of Rösi and Helga, who work under those names alone. The project started in 2020, originally as a trio, after the three met at an Orange Sector concert. The third member produced the beats on the first two releases and left the line-up; Rösi and Helga have continued as a duo since 2024. Their first release was the six-track EP “Versuchen ist der erste Schritt zum Scheitern” in 2022, with the songs “Kohle”, “Freddy”, “Tanzen”, “Tempus fugit”, “Mutter hat verboten” and a “Tanzen Nacht Mix”. The EP “Is das schon Kunst ?!” followed in 2024. Both remain on the duo’s own Bandcamp page. The two singers alternate lead vocals across the material rather than splitting the songs between them, a method they carry over to the album. “Der Charme des Stumpfen” is their first full-length record and their first release on a label, and it arrives with two outside remixers attached, from Zweite Jugend and Aktion : Fiasko.

It is the second single from “Casablanca Nights 2: The Unveiled Chapter”, a twelve-track album due on 30 October 2026 and open for pre-order since 21 August. Casablanca Nights 2: The Unveiled Chapter by Johan Ageb
items.body: Every track on the new Johan Agebjörn album has a different singer on it. The Swedish producer, best known for Sally Shapiro, releases “Falling” featuring Yota on 4 September 2026 as a digital single through Blanco y Negro Music and his own Johan Agebjörn Music. It is the second single from “Casablanca Nights 2: The Unveiled Chapter”, a twelve-track album due on 30 October 2026 and open for pre-order since 21 August. Casablanca Nights 2: The Unveiled Chapter by Johan Agebjörn Yota is a Stockholm-born vocalist and songwriter, credited on Discogs under the name Jotta Hautanen, who now lives in Paris. She described hearing the demo for the first time on a walk in the park: “I recall listening to the demo of ‘Falling’ that Johan sent to me during a walk in the park and it was instantly playing on every emotional chord within me. The progressive and slightly subtle intensity in it just blew me away. It felt right. It was one of those rare moments when something just seems tailored to find its way through every little cell in your body and mind and connect with you. The tension this track carries is quite massive, especially as it’s delivered (at least partially) in a subtle and soft manner. The fact that it also has the elements that I naturally feel drawn to like the whispery and suggestive vocals and an instrumental that is melodic and deep, confirmed my initial feeling even more which was that this just had to happen.” Johan Agebjörn pairs a different singer with every track Agebjörn produced the whole of “Casablanca Nights 2: The Unveiled Chapter” himself and gave each of the twelve tracks its own guest. “Falling” with Yota opens the record, followed by “Beautiful Stranger” with Little Boots, which came out as the first single on 21 August 2026. The rest of the running order is “Fakesnow” with R Missing, “Substitute For Love” with Ellen Andrea Wang, “My Only One” with Fred Ventura, “Hush Hush Baby” with Nina, “Waiting For Magic” with Dana Jean Phoenix and Mikael Ögren, a 2026 mix of “Have You Ever Been In Love” with Tom Hooker, “Love On Ice” with Ryan Paris and Sally Shapiro, “Filled Me Up” with Bunny X, “Will You Be Home For Christmas” with Dana Jean Phoenix, and “Nightbows” with R. Missing. The album is a sequel to “Casablanca Nights”, which Paper Bag Records released in 2011 and which used the same method of a rotating cast of vocalists. About Johan Agebjörn Johan Agebjörn is a producer and songwriter based in Lund, Sweden, who has made italo disco and synth-pop since the mid-2000s. He started Sally Shapiro in 2006 with the track “I’ll Be By Your Side”, and the project’s debut album “Disco Romance” came out on Diskokaine. Later Sally Shapiro records moved through Paper Bag Records and Permanent Vacation, including “My Guilty Pleasure” in August 2009, before the duo signed to Italians Do It Better for “Sally Shapiro” in 2022 and “Ready to Live a Lie” in May 2025. In September 2023 they released a cover of the Pet Shop Boys’ “Rent”. Outside Sally Shapiro, Agebjörn has released solo albums and produced for other singers. “Casablanca Nights” appeared on Paper Bag Records in 2011. He worked with Samantha Fox on “Hot Boy” in 2018 and with Loney Dear on “The Leftovers”, and remixed Annie’s “Swedish Kiss” in 2014. He and Yota had already worked together before this album, on the 2024 EP “Universe In Flames”. “Casablanca Nights 2: The Unveiled Chapter” is his first album under his own name since that collaboration, and “Falling” is the track the pair placed first on it.

items.body: San Diego synthpop trio Twin Ritual released the single “Suffocate” on 28 August 2026. It is the band’s first new recording since “Allie” in May 2023 and is out on Bandcamp. Hannah Mahute wrote the lyrics and sings. Anthony Ramirez, who also plays in Glass Spells, handles synthesizers, bass and drum machine, and Antonio Estrada plays guitars. The band wrote the song together. Vocals and guitars were recorded at Chateau Trumfio, and Dave Trumfio mixed and mastered the track. Suffocate by Twin Ritual How ‘Suffocate’ sounds The arrangement runs on a steady drum-machine pulse and wide synthesizer lines, with Estrada’s guitar set in open, measured phrases that alternate between texture and lead melody. Mahute sings in the centre of that space, moving between a soft delivery and a sharper one. The song deals with staying beside someone who is withdrawing into their own pain, and with the limits of what patience can do about it. Dave Trumfio’s involvement links the single to a long run of American independent rock records. He founded Kingsize Soundlabs in Chicago’s Wicker Park in the 1990s and moved the studio to Los Angeles in 2000, and has produced or engineered for Wilco, Built to Spill, My Morning Jacket and OK Go. Here he handled the mix and the master. About Twin Ritual Twin Ritual are a three-piece from San Diego, California, built around Hannah Mahute’s vocals, Anthony Ramirez’s synthesizers and rhythm programming, and Antonio Estrada’s guitar. Their music mixes synthpop with atmospheric guitar and a slow-burning, cinematic pace. The band’s first release, the single “Angry”, appeared on 12 October 2017. The “Hand Through The Mist EP” followed on 9 February 2018. “Norma Jean” arrived as a single on 29 October 2019, and “Allie” on 5 May 2023. Ramirez is also a member of Glass Spells, the San Diego synthpop project Side-Line has covered separately. Twin Ritual’s own releases have all been issued independently rather than through a label. “Suffocate” ends a three-year gap in the band’s discography. No album or EP has been announced to follow it.

items.body: Stockholm post-punk trio Then Comes Silence have released a behind-the-scenes documentary on the making of their “Judgement Day” video, filmed and edited by the Swedish video maker Marzipan Moonlight. The film follows the studio shoot for the single, which came out on 7 August 2026 through Metropolis Records as the first track from the band’s eighth album, “Requiem Ballroom”. The music video itself was directed by Damon Zurawski of Future Legend Films and staged as a live performance in a photo studio, with invited extras dancing around the band. Marzipan Moonlight’s film documents that day from the floor: the setup, the repeated takes, and the friends and members of Stockholm’s goth community who filled the room as extras. Vocalist and bassist Alex Svenson describes the shoot as closer to a concert than to a film set: “We gave a performance in the photo studio when shooting the music video. It was like a regular concert with the extras dancing around the band. People seemed to enjoy being involved in the making of this video – it’s easy to dance to and has a good dynamic.” Drummer Jonas Fransson accounts for one of the smaller participants: “We invited a bunch of friends to join us for the music video shoot, and one of them happens to be a 16-year-old Miniature Pinscher. He is almost completely deaf, so he didn’t mind walking around the studio while we were playing.” Judgement Day by Then Comes Silence “Judgement Day” is on Bandcamp, Spotify and Apple Music. The full background to the single and to “Requiem Ballroom”, which is due on 20 November 2026 through Metropolis Records, is covered in Side-Line’s earlier report on Then Comes Silence release ‘Judgement Day’, announce album ‘Requiem Ballroom’. Svenson has described the track as a nod to Killing Joke, and Johan Lange of Agent Side Grinder plays synthesizer on one album track. Then Comes Silence tour dates The band open a European run in Belgium on 11 September and close in Stockholm in October: 11 September 2026 – Glain, Belgium – Deux Ours 12 September 2026 – Rotterdam-Albrandswaard, Netherlands – Baroeg Open Air 13 September 2026 – Rennes, France – Brewklyn 14 September 2026 – Paris, France – Le Chinois 15 September 2026 – Rezé, France – Cold Crash 16 September 2026 – Lyon, France – Rock N’Eat 17 September 2026 – Marseille, France – Le Molotov 18 September 2026 – Torino, Italy – Ziggy Club 19 September 2026 – Castelfranco Veneto, Italy – Sale Improve 20 September 2026 – Prague, Czechia – Subzero 24 October 2026 – Stockholm, Sweden – Kollektivet Livet Tickets are routed through the band’s own tour links page. About Then Comes Silence Then Comes Silence formed in Stockholm in 2012 around vocalist, bassist and songwriter Alex Svenson, who has written the lyrics and music throughout the project’s history. The line-up narrowed to a trio in 2022 and now pairs Svenson with drummer Jonas Fransson and guitarist Hugo Zombie. The band issued the self-titled “Then Comes Silence” in 2012 and “Then Comes Silence II” in 2013, followed by “Nyctophilian” on Novoton in 2015. “Blood” arrived in 2017 through Nuclear Blast, “Machine” in 2020 through Metropolis Records and SPV, and “Hunger” in 2022 through Nexilis Records and Schubert Music. “Trickery” followed in 2024 on Metropolis Records. Sonic Seducer named “Blood”, “Machine”, “Hunger” and “Trickery” album of the month on their release. The group has toured widely across Europe, North America and Latin America, sharing stages with Fields of the Nephilim, Clan of Xymox, The Chameleons and Pink Turns Blue, and has played M’era Luna, Wave-Gotik-Treffen, Amphi Festival, Castle Party and W-Festival. “Requiem Ballroom” is split into two halves, “Ballroom” and “Requiem”. Jon Bordon mixed the first, Tom van Heesch the second, and Svante Forsbäck mastered the record at Chartmakers. D.K. Griftegaard and Jonas Fransson made the cover artwork. The behind-the-scenes film is the second piece of video the band have put out around “Judgement Day”, ahead of the album on 20 November.

Jacob’s Studio and the making of ‘Strange Times’ The sessions ran for five weeks at Jacob’s Studio, in Ridgeway House
items.body: The Chameleons, the post-punk band from Middleton, Greater Manchester, released their third studio album “Strange Times” on 1 September 1986 through Geffen Records. The album turns 40 this year. David M. Allen produced it. North America received the record four weeks later, on 29 September 1986, with a bonus LP attached to initial vinyl copies. Jacob’s Studio and the making of ‘Strange Times’ The sessions ran for five weeks at Jacob’s Studio, in Ridgeway House near Farnham, Surrey. Mark Saunders engineered, with Paul Crocket and Beki Field assisting and adding piano. Reg Smithies drew the cover, as he had for every Chameleons release since the band’s first single. The line-up was Mark Burgess on bass and vocals, Dave Fielding on lead guitar and ARP String Ensemble, Smithies on rhythm guitar and John Lever on drums and percussion. Ten tracks run 52:09: “Mad Jack,” “Caution,” “Tears” (original arrangement), “Soul in Isolation,” “Swamp Thing,” “Time/The End of Time,” “Seriocity,” “In Answer,” “Childhood” and “I’ll Remember.” The vinyl carried no B side. Both sides were credited instead as Side A and Side A+. Asked where the record sits among the band’s albums, Burgess gave a short answer in the sleeve notes on the band’s website: “Strange Times is my favourite.” Two singles came out of the sessions. “Tears” arrived first, on 16 June 1986, in a version credited as the full arrangement, electric where the album take is acoustic and ends differently. “Swamp Thing” followed on release day itself, backed by a cover of David Bowie’s “John, I’m Only Dancing.” A promotional 12″ issued the same year paired “Mad Jack” with “Time/The End of Time” and a reading of the Beatles’ “Tomorrow Never Knows.” The bonus LP bundled with early North American pressings held six non-album tracks; the American cassette split those across both sides. No CD edition existed until 1993, when Geffen released a two-disc set in the UK and Germany and an American single disc that dropped “Ever After” to fit. Reissues have continued since: a Japanese CD on 25 February 2004, a Music on CD two-disc edition in Europe on 20 March 2020, a Moochin’ About double LP on coloured vinyl on 28 October 2022, and remastered 2CD and 3LP editions through Blue Apple Music on 3 May 2024. The Spotify edition carries 16 tracks, the album plus the bonus material. About The Chameleons The Chameleons formed in Middleton, Greater Manchester, in 1981, when Mark Burgess joined guitarists Reg Smithies and Dave Fielding. Burgess had played with the Cliches; Smithies and Fielding came from Years. They started as a trio without a drummer, took on fellow Middletonian Brian Schofield, and settled on John Lever of Dukinfield, previously of the Politicians. Martin Jackson, formerly of Magazine, covered the drum stool during 1982 and 1983 while Lever took a sabbatical. A 1981 session for John Peel led to a contract with Epic Records, which issued the debut single “In Shreds” in March 1982 with Steve Lillywhite producing, and dropped the band shortly after over disagreements about packaging and image. Statik Records, a Virgin subsidiary, picked the group up and released the debut album “Script of the Bridge” in 1983, a record Side-Line covered in The Chameleons’ ‘Script of the Bridge’ turns 43 on 8 August. Statik’s ownership disqualified the album from the UK independent charts, and MCA cut four songs from the American edition, a decision the band objected to. The second album, “What Does Anything Mean? Basically,” followed on Statik in 1985. Constant touring and the work of manager Tony Fletcher brought the band to Geffen Records, and to “Strange Times.” Fletcher died of cardiac arrest in 1987, and with a rift already open between Burgess and Fielding, the group broke up. The EP “Tony Fletcher Walked on Water…. La La La La La-La La-La-La,” recorded in 1987 and named for him, appeared in 1990. Burgess and Lever formed The Sun and the Moon, releasing one album on Geffen in 1988; Smithies and Fielding formed The Reegs, who put out two albums on Imaginary Records in 1991 and 1992. The Chameleons reconvened in January 2000 for a run of shows at The Witchwood in Ashton-under-Lyne, issued the acoustic album “Strip” that May, then “Why Call It Anything” in 2001 and a second unplugged record, “This Never Ending Now,” in 2002. Renewed tensions ended the reunion in early 2003. From 2009 Burgess and Lever played the catalogue as ChameleonsVox. Lever died on 13 March 2017, aged 55. Burgess and Smithies reformed the band under its own name in May 2021 with guitarist Chris Oliver and drummer Stephen Rice, recording “Edge Sessions (Live from the Edge),” released on 25 April 2022 by Metropolis Records. The current line-up adds drummer Todd Demma and keyboardist Danny Ashberry. New material followed after a two-decade gap, covered here in The Chameleons release first new material in over 20 years: ‘Where Are You?’ and The Chameleons release ‘Tomorrow Remember Yesterday’ EP with re-recorded early tracks – Out now, ahead of the single reported in Chameleons release new single ‘Saviours Are A Dangerous Thing’ via Metropolis Records and the dates listed in Chameleons announce European ‘Arctic Moon’ Tour 2025. The fifth studio album, “Arctic Moon,” was released on 12 September 2025 through Metropolis Records. Forty years on, “Strange Times” remains the last album the original quartet finished together.

items.body: Polish witchpop and darkwave act Agnis released a cover of “Mile Deep Hollow” on 28 August 2026. The single-track digital release is her first new recording since the 2025 album “Gothess” and is available on Bandcamp. The original appeared on IAMX‘s third album “Kingdom of Welcome Addiction”, released on 19 May 2009. Agnis keeps the song’s structure and moves it into her own setting of darkpop atmospheres and electronics. She describes the approach in one line on the release page: “Some songs don’t need to be rewritten, only re-enchanted.” Mile Deep Hollow (IAMX cover) by AGNIS Where the Agnis cover sits in her release run This is not her first cover. “Gothess” included a version of Britney Spears’ “Toxic”, and she has since released a reading of Lady Gaga’s “Abracadabra”. “Mile Deep Hollow” is the second IAMX-adjacent point of contact for Side-Line readers this year: the band’s Chris Corner released the single “Artificial Innocence” in February 2026 ahead of a European tour. Agnis remains signed to darkTunes Music Group, the German label that issued her debut. No album has been announced as the follow-up to “Gothess”. About Agnis Agnis is the solo project of Polish singer and producer Agnieszka Leśna, who previously performed with Desdemona and with her own band Red Storm. She works under the witchpop label, mixing darkwave and witch house electronics with Wiccan imagery. Side-Line first covered the project in January 2022, when Agnis released the single and video for “Sol Invictus”. The debut album “Oneness” followed on 25 March 2022 through darkTunes, running ten tracks: “I Am The Light”, “Gray Magic”, “Transubstantiation”, “Let’s Get Magical”, “Sol Invictus”, “Light And Fire”, “Polyhymnia”, “True Self”, “Slavic Witch” and “Cosmic Goddess”. The second album, “Gothess”, arrived on 4 April 2025 with eleven tracks, including “Antipriest”, “Dark Dancer”, “Halloween Night”, “Baba Jaga”, “Elixir”, “Creatures of the Night”, “Vamp”, “Incantation” and the title track. A remix collection, “Gothess Remixes”, followed, with reworks by Basszilla, Antibody, Freaky Mind, The Silverblack, Chem, Prophette, Cattac, White Ritual, Vioflesh and C Z A R I N A. The standalone single “Wicked Witch” came out on 21 November 2025. In 2026 she released “Satisfaction” with label mates Extize and Basszilla, and toured Germany and Austria with Extize. “Mile Deep Hollow” is her first release since that collaboration, and her first cover of a track from the industrial and electronic rock catalogue rather than the pop charts.

items.body: And One released “Bodypop” on 1 September 2006 through Out Of Line in Europe, with a US edition following on 7 November 2006 via Metropolis Records. The ninth studio album by the Berlin electropop/EBM band turns 20 this year. It was produced by co-founder Steve Naghavi and followed 2003’s “Aggressor,” the band’s previous studio album. The German CD edition runs 12 tracks: “Mein Anfang,” “Military Fashion Show,” “Enjoy The Unknown,” “So Klingt Liebe,” “The Sound Of Believer,” “Body Company,” “Traumfrau,” “Stand The Pain,” “Sexkeit,” “Love You To The End,” “The Dream” and “Dein Ende.” A limited “Bodypop”/”Frontfeuer” CD/EP bundle added five further tracks: “Rearming Strafbomber,” “Master Master,” “A Kind of Deutsch,” “Steine Sind Steine” and “The Force.” Band members Steve Naghavi, Chris Ruiz and Gio van Oli are credited as performers on the album, which was mastered at Master & Servant. Out Of Line has since reissued “Bodypop” on vinyl in 2018 and 2023 and on cassette in 2024. Two singles preceded the album and one followed it: “Military Fashion Show” (19 May 2006), which reached number one on the Deutsche Alternative Charts, “So Klingt Liebe” (14 July 2006), which peaked at number three, and “Traumfrau” (1 December 2006). Side-Line reported on a double-vinyl reissue of “Bodypop” in 2018. About And One And One formed in Berlin, Germany, in 1989, founded by Steve Naghavi and Chris Ruiz, who met at a Berlin nightclub and initially performed under the name Body Project. Alex Two joined before the band’s 1991 debut. The single “Metal Hammer” (1990) became a club hit ahead of the debut album “Anguish,” released on Machinery Records in 1991, the year And One won a regional “Best New Artist” award. Three further albums followed on Machinery: “Flop!” (1992), “Spot” (1993) and “I.S.T.” (1994). And One signed to Virgin Schallplatten in the mid-1990s, releasing “Nordhausen” (1997), “9.9.99 9 Uhr” (1999), “Virgin Superstar” (2000) and “Aggressor” (2003). Chris Ruiz left the band in 1992 and returned in 2001; Joke Jay and Rick Schah joined the lineup across the late 1990s and 2000s. The band moved to Out Of Line for Europe and Metropolis Records for the United States starting with “Bodypop” in 2006. And One continued with “Tanzomat” (2011), “S.T.O.P.” (2012) and “Magnet” (2014), released alongside companion albums “Propeller” and “Achtung 80” as part of a “Magnet Trilogie.” Chris Ruiz left the band again in 2011 to co-found Pakt with Gio van Oli and Chad Hauger. Steve Naghavi remains the band’s constant member; Nico Wieditz has performed with the band since 2012.

items.body: I walk through fire with my head held high Is that really such a crime? Leaving a faith can redraw the borders of reality. Certainties that once governed time, guilt, desire, and the fate of the self fall away at once, leaving freedom inseparable from vertigo. A person must decide which pieces of the old world deserve burial, which can be carried forward, and how to inhabit a life no longer mapped by inherited answers. Portland post-punk quartet Nyx Division enters that exposed territory with By Design, a new single rooted in vocalist Domino Monet’s experience of escaping the Mormon church. Released ahead of the band’s East Coast dates, including a set at NYC’s A Murder of Crows, the song follows the collapse of a prescribed worldview into the frightening, sensuous freedom of choosing what comes next. Monet describes the subject as “the liminal expanse between awe and terror,” where ontological loss meets the exhilaration of reconstructing a world from its broken pieces. By Design opens with acoustic guitar and a dry, vibraslap-like rattle, setting a touch of spaghetti-Western theater ahead of Monet’s first lines. The full band soon bears down through Justin Cory’s heavy guitar figures and Mason Wilkinson’s firm percussion, while Alex Rivas sends a nimble bassline dancing underneath. As the initial force relaxes into a melodic groove, the track takes on a psychedelic hue. Cory’s guitar reaches toward the broad alt-rock and shoegaze sweep of bands like Catherine Wheel while retaining the core rhythmic pull of 80s post-punk. Monet supplies the song’s greatest sense of scale. Her held notes tremble with heat and conviction, drawing upon the commanding tradition of women rock singers from the 1970s and ’80s. Fire, memory, sin, and survival pass through the lyrics as lived conditions rather than decoration. The repeated title carries a productive reversal: language often used to justify a divinely ordered universe becomes a declaration of self-authorship. Design now belongs to the person who endured the old plan and walked away with the right to make another. That tension gives the track its lift. The music recognizes the cost of departure while making room for appetite, beauty, and volition. Its dance-floor momentum feels connected to the body’s return after years spent beneath doctrine, and its desert atmosphere suggests an open horizon where terror and possibility share the same immense sky. Listen to By Design below: By Design by Nyx Division Formed in Portland in 2021, Nyx Division brings post-punk, goth, and rock ’n’ roll into a muscular, romantic union. The group released the Dark Star EP in 2022, followed by the 2025 singles Soldier of Love and Midnight Lights. By Design expands that approach through acoustic color, psychedelic breadth, and a hard-earned sense of release. Nyx Division now heads across the East Coast for four early-September appearances. The band shares the Philadelphia, Worcester, and Cambridge dates with eX-Tradition. Their September 4 stop places them at New York’s Bowery Ballroom for the first of the festival’s two main nights at A Murder of Crows XI, appearing alongside Anja Huwe, Rosegarden Funeral Party, Creux Lies, and Guilty Strangers. Nyx Division East Coast Tour Dates September 3 — Philadelphia, PA — Cousin Danny’s Lounge, with eX-Tradition, NRG, and Subtle Body September 4 — New York, NY — Bowery Ballroom, A Murder of Crows XI September 5 — Worcester, MA — Distant Castle, with eX-Tradition September 6 — Cambridge, MA — Middle East Upstairs, with eX-Tradition Follow Nyx Division: Instagram Bandcamp The post “I Feel Like a Star Again” — Nyx Division Become the Architects of Their Own Destiny in “By Design” appeared first on Post-Punk.com.

items.album: New Zealand Post-Punk Outfit Trauma Party Confronts the Political Circus in Fiery Video for “Roll Up (It’s the New Truth)”
items.excerpt: They’re bringing their violence They’re bringing their bile They’re juggling their words They’re bringing the new truth Trauma Party have found the right instrument for 2026: a busted carnival loudspeaker wired straight into the national nervous system. items.body: They’re bringing their violence They’re bringing their bile They’re juggling their words They’re bringing the new truth Trauma Party have found the right instrument for 2026: a busted carnival loudspeaker wired straight into the national nervous system. Roll Up (It’s the New Truth), the final video single drawn from the New Zealand group’s debut EP Because You’ve Been Good, barrels forward on rolling drums and blackened guitar, turning political disgust into a carnival bark that grows more feverish with every repetition. There is some of The Fall’s sour wit in the delivery, some Killing Joke in the pressure underneath, and a trace of Sham 69 in the gang-minded force of the refrain. Then the psychedelic stink rolls in. The Crazy World of Arthur Brown feels close at hand, while the guitars occasionally carry the broad, wounded sweep associated with The Chameleons. Trauma Party throws these ingredients into a garage-rock furnace and lets the song stagger around like a circus tent caught in a riot. The lyrics present authoritarian politics as cheap entertainment turned lethal. A fat orange clown presides over cages, bile, violence, snake oil, obedient freaks, and language mangled until falsehood becomes official reality. The joke keeps curdling because the circus imagery is funny for roughly half a second before its implications land. Spectacle becomes governance, repetition becomes persuasion, and the crowd is expected to applaud while vocabulary itself is dragged behind the tent and beaten senseless. “This song is not quiet; it screams at us all to wake up and beware ‘the new truth’ and the surreality of alternative facts,” the band says. “It’s a fiery post-punk alert from the fringes, illustrating the strength of art and music as tools of resistance.” Buddy Olson pushes the point further with a statement whose terse menace could have been painted across a barricade: “The privileged are few. We have them surrounded. Don’t let them escape. Hold them accountable.” The accompanying video gives the song an appropriately lawless setting. Filmed outside The Woolshed, Trauma Party’s clubhouse at the Waiheke Dirt Track, the band perform beneath a cold moon amid fire, smoke, and Molotov cocktails. Cars continue passing in the background, an almost comic detail that makes the scene more disturbing: apocalypse as roadside attraction, fury blazing a few metres away while ordinary traffic keeps moving, while everyone is expected to call the wreckage progress again. There is a Mad Max quality to the imagery, crossed with the scruffy end-times fatalism of A Boy and His Dog, yet the cheap-thrills destruction carries political purpose. Watch the video for Roll Up (It’s The New Truth) below: Trauma Party closes their EP Because You’ve Been Good by making the circus grotesque, psychedelic, and dangerously catchy. The tents are up, the clown is talking, the audience is already inside, and somewhere behind the music somebody is selling the lie as admission price. Listen to Roll Up (It’s The New Truth) below and order the single here. items.body: Tuğçe Şenoğul Atlas self-released There’s precious little information in English about Turkish vocalist Tuğçe Şenoğul. Aside from references to her time as one half of Seni Görmem İmkansız, and a few scattered write-ups about various collabs, it’s hard to find much reliable on the Istanbul-based artist. With that said, her streams on Spotify and Turkish language coverage certainly attest to some degree of popularity in her home country, with her new album Atlas (following from EP of the same name a few years back) demonstrating an intriguing mixture of modern electropop and traditional folk music. How that works in practice is fairly straightforward; on tracks like “Serseri” and “Cennet” Şenoğul mixes smoky, trip-hoppy production with strings, percussion and horns, all blended with a remarkable smoothness that speaks to the overall earthy and organic vibe of the compositions. Not every track relies on the mixture of traditional and electronic instruments – the lovely opener “Kırık Hikaye” is entirely made up of electronic ambiences, while “Bu Gece” is largely a simple piano based composition – their deployment a testament to the more measured and sensuous vibe of the instrumentals. It’s of course easy for the non-Turkish listener to get caught up in the novelty of hearing these sounds and musical approaches brought together, but there’s actually an interesting tension in how complex the arrangements and songwriting performance are, and Şenoğul’s presence as a vocalist. The record is very much at its best when the instrumentation gets out of her way and lets her take all the focus. The title track features a lovely mixture of percussion and some very interesting stringed instruments along with its throbbing electronic pulse, but it’s all about hearing how she slides between each different element, forceful without needing to belt it out or even change the urgency of her delivery. The tracks with a slightly more traditional structure end up being a mixed bag; “Sensin Bunlara Sebep” is a more traditional pop take on Turkish folk but is far less intriguing than the loungey, Collide-esque sounds of “Hatıramızla”, delivered with a reserved but coy wink. While you’ve got a few tracks in the mix like “Aşk Deli” that could fit on a darkwave dancefloor alongside Kite, the real appeal of Atlas lies in its warm, enveloping production and the power of Tuğçe Şenoğul as a performer. Even without knowing a lick about the themes and topics of these songs, she cleanly communicates love, sorrow, loss and resolve, picking her spots to hold back, where she employs her full range, and knowing how each bit of phrasing and inflection effects the whole. Buy it. Atlas by Tuğçe Şenoğul The post Tuğçe Şenoğul, “Atlas” appeared first on I Die: You Die.

items.body: One Eleven Heavy’s Nick Mitchell Maiato’s tightened take on Cosmic Americana highlights all of the best qualities of this nebulous genre. This is perhaps most evident on his new album, Náquera, which goes heavy on the choogle, while still gleaming with ear-catching hooks and hyper-focused songwriting. This is Mitchell displaying his ability to create radio friendly music that doesn’t betray his head heritage nor his love for jamming. This winning combination of the loose and the carefully constructed makes songs like the very James Gang-like opening cut, “Two Right Feet,” or the following track, the rollicking slice of honky-tonk that is “Critical Mass,” especially righteous tunes. The sound on this record might be the closest Mitchell has come to sounding like One Eleven Heavy as a purely solo artist. The contributions of former members James Toth and Hans Chew certainly helps. Yet, this album goes even further into the weeds of country rock music than OEH ever attempted. This is a fun record full of grooving ear candy that fans of the Grateful Dead, Sir Douglas Quintet and Leon Russel would immediately love. With bouncy upbeat rhythms, classically addictive melodies and heaps of roadhouse band charm, the songs here feel like the very essence of stoned Americana music, and rough and tumble good times. This particular aspect of the record is just one of several ways that it’s linked to the Dead’s influence. Songs like “Riki Rachtman,” with its twinkling Keith Godchaux-like piano work, warm pedal steel and sweet harmonies, rambles and chugs along like a lost Europe 72 cut. Yet, perhaps the most unexpected connection to the legacy of Jerry and the gang, is the guest appearance of Bob Bralove, former midi-engineer and auxiliary musician for the Dead, who cut a searing organ solo on “Critical Mass.” Yet the most noticeable shift in Mitchell’s music is the addition of horns that adorn this record ever so tastefully. The 70’s country rock vibe of this album absolutely welcomes the brass, especially on “The Angle,” which feels close to something Allen Toussaint would have contributed to a swinging Robbie Robertson tune. The touch of soul from these horns is the icing on the cake that is the party vibe of Náquera. Grab yourself a copy and join the party today.

9月27日はあなたの星座で満月。ひとつのことが成就し、クライマックスを迎えるタイミングです。 ラッキーアクションは手づくりのスイーツ作り。甘いものが好きではないのなら、ソルティーなお菓子や野菜を使ったおやつ作りなど。丁寧に手順を踏んで完成品を作る訓練になります。 今月の牡羊座におすすめのラッキー・アルバム：ミッシャ・マイスキー『祈り〜20世紀のメロディ』 牡羊座の2026下半期の運勢 牡牛座（4月21日～5月21日） あなたの支配星・金星が対人関係とパートナーシップのハウスに入り、今年いっぱい順行と逆行を繰り返しながらパートナーの問題に発展や波紋を投げかけてきます。公の場での上下関係に変化が起こることもありそうですが、一番大きなことは私生活面でのパートナーシップで現れてきそう。今年前半までの不安定なムードが収まってきているだけに、何か小さなストレスを頻繁に送ってくる相手や、経済面にだらしなく計画性に欠ける相手とは、将来をともに生きるモチベーションが激減してしまいそう。牡牛座自身の価値観や未来像がはっきりしてくるときだけに、新たな出会いもやってきそう。今よりもっと、居心地のいい相手を選んでいいのです。 仕事面では、美的な感覚を問われることが多くなり、仕上げる速さよりも出来栄えを重視して正解。細かいプロセスにも心をこめること。 今月の牡牛座におすすめのラッキー・アルバム：熊木夕茉が歌う『武満徹のうた』 牡牛座の2026年下半期の運勢 双子座（5月22日～6月21日） 物事を決定したり、選択したりするときに「できるだけ選択肢は多いほうがいい」と考えるのは、双子座特有の感覚です。この季節も、いろいろなことを調べたり経験したりして、情報を集めていくことになりそうですが、これまで以上に「実感」「体感」という要素を重視して。人を選ぶときもデータや肩書に左右されず、直観的なものを重視すると間違いがないようです。 あなたの仕事や表現、コミュニケーション・スタイルにおいても「有機的であること」を大切にして。「自分は有能なのだから、何も言わなくてもそのうち皆が理解するだろう」といったアプローチは沈没してしまいそうです。感情を表し、表情を取り戻して、クールな態度に偏らないこと。仕事も心をこめて、誰か任せにしないこと。 ハイテクの天体・天王星は9月11日から双子座で逆行をスタートし、AI任せの仕事術には危機感が起こりそう。クリエイティブ面は、AIに丸投げしないことです。 今月の双子座におすすめのラッキー・アルバム：マリア・ドゥエニャスによる『ハイフェッツへのオマージュ』 双子座の2026年下半期の運勢 蟹座（6月22日～7月23日） エネルギーの星・火星は蟹座を進行中。多忙期は9月28日まで続きますが、今月の特徴としては、今まで上の世代で詰まっていた順番がようやく回ってきて、センターで活躍できたり、主役級のポジションを与えられたりとハイライト的な華やかさをともなう運気になりそう。「あなたはすごい！」と近づいてきた相手には、愛想よく振る舞って。営業的にも、フレンドリーなキャラクターでいることで蟹座は大きく得をします。 過去6年間にわたって、かなり「疲れる働き方」をしてきた蟹座ですが、ここからは得意なこと、周囲からスムーズに賞賛されることに絞って活動していいかもしれません。「きついし苦手だけど、こなさなければならない」仕事は、もう十分にやってきたのではないでしょうか。プライベートは十分な休息を。温泉旅行吉。ワンランク上の宿でゴージャス体験をしてみては？ 今月の蟹座におすすめのラッキー・アルバム：グリュミオーが奏でる『ルクー：ヴァイオリン・ソナタ、他』 蟹座の2026年下半期の運勢 獅子座（7月24日～8月23日） 楽しい夏のお祭り気分が収まり、身辺を整理整頓しながら日々の仕事に集中する季節に入りました。2026年前半は、トラブルも幸運も一気にやってきて、交通整理が大変だったのでは？ 太陽が獅子座から去った9月、落ち着いて過去に起こったことや自分の未来について考える時間が与えられます。 今こなしている仕事についても「社会でどのように機能しているのか」「自分の天命と一致しているのか」と考えることがありそう。獅子座は「歓び」の星座です。あまりに義務に偏り過ぎると、この先望まない展開がやってくるかも。「頑張るのとは別の方法はないか？」と誰かに相談するのもいいでしょう。木星が獅子座を加護している現在、方向転換には適しているタイミングです。 対人関係の課題は、じっくりゆっくりと解決を。10年、20年単位で時間をさかのぼって考えることもありそうです。このテーマに関しては、自己中心的であっては解決できないものです。 今月の獅子座におすすめのラッキー・アルバム：辻井伸行『THE BEST』 獅子座の2026年下半期の運勢 乙女座（8月24日～9月22日） 働き者の乙女座ですが、今年に限ってなかなか「働きモード」スイッチが入りづらくなっているのでは？ 自由時間の楽しさ、遊ぶことの有意義さに目覚めた今のあなたは、無味乾燥なルーティンワークに戻りたくない、と考えているかもしれません。新しいモチベーションを得た人から、仕事への意欲を復帰させていくことになりそうですが、「それが見つからない」という乙女座も焦らなくてOKです。「私はまだ夏休みを延長して楽しんでいて、自分の心身をリラックスさせる必要があるんです」と主張するのもあり。それを許さない仕事環境もあるでしょう。いろいろ考え事も多くなりそうです。積年の過労モードを考えるなら、3か月くらいの休みは欲しいところですが、仕事そのものに楽しみや創造性を感じられるようになったなら、職場に戻ってもOK。 9月11日はあなたの星座で新月となり、重大なリセットが行なわれるかもしれません。髪型を変えたり、服装をバージョン・アップさせるなどは推奨アクション。 今月のあなたにおすすめのラッキー・アルバム：インバル指揮『ブルックナー：交響曲第4番』 乙女座の2026年下半期の運勢 天秤座（9月23日～10月23日） 地味で堅実な日々が続いていましたが、あなたの揺るがない存在感は多くの人々から一目置かれてきました。派手さや大袈裟なアプローチを嫌う天秤座は、少し見えづらいところで集団の成功を支えてきたようです。公正さを大切にする天秤座に反して、身内だけを贔屓にしたり、排他的になったりする動きも近くにはあったようですが、あなたはそこに対しても寛容な態度をとってきたのでしょう。 太陽が天秤座に入る9月24日以降、あなたのポリシーが正しかったことが大々的に認められるはず。世の中は性急に利益を求めたがっていますが、あなたは経験上「それは空しいことである」と知っているようです。強い味方になってくれるのは、バックグラウンドが似ている相手。同じ教育方針で育ってきた人物です。 プライベートでは自然と親しむ小旅行、癒しの旅がおすすめ。香りによるリラックスも◎。針葉樹のアロマなど。 今月の天秤座におすすめのラッキーアルバム：クルト・マズア指揮『マーラー：交響曲第9番』 天秤座の2026年下半期の運勢 蠍座（10月24日～11月22日） 「案ずるより産むが易し」の月。夏の間念入りに準備してきたことの「本番」を迎える蠍座は、緊張よりもそれを迎えたことの楽しさや喜びに包まれそう。あなたはしっかりと時間を重ね、精神面での成熟を達成してきました。そうした根深いあり方に対して、2026年前半はチープな合理性を優先させる傾向があったため、蠍座としては「活躍の場があまりない」と感じることがあったかも。 9月11日に天王星の逆行が始まると、蠍座の揺るがないアプローチが再評価され、大きなステージに上がる機会が増えてきそうです。同時に金星も蠍座に入り、蠍座の「愛するなら本気で向き合い、末永く愛し合いたい」という態度が報われる流れに。仕事や人生修養の場でも「恩師」を大切にする蠍座の心が、皆から支持されるでしょう。オフタイムはインテリアに凝って、よりエネルギーに満ちた部屋作りを。 今月の蠍座におすすめのラッキー・アルバム：ジャン=フランソワ・パイヤール『パッヘルベルのカノン〜バロック名曲集』 蠍座の2026年下半期の運勢 射手座（11月23日～12月21日） 自由度がアップし、規則や義務に侵食されることなく「やりたいこと」を究められる季節です。射手座自身、新しい資格や免許を取ることに興味が湧いたり、行動範囲をどんどん広げていきたいと思うよう。周囲もそんなあなたを見て「パワフルで面白い！」と応援してくれそうです。 仕事とも遊びともつかないアドベンチャーも吉。射手座の天才的思考で、簡単には「完成」とならないプロジェクトも生まれそうですが、それは「遊び」が発端になるでしょう。単独でもグループでも楽しめるときなので、仕事もプライベートも自由にパートナーをキャスティングして。 親孝行や祖父・祖母孝行には素晴らしいリターンあり。恋愛は、パートナーのハウスの天王星が逆行をはじめ、電撃的な出会いから始まった縁は少しずつ冷静さを取り戻していく段階に。 今月の射手座におすすめのラッキー・アルバム：シプリアン・カツァリスが弾く『バッハ：ピアノ協奏曲集』 射手座の2026年下半期の運勢 山羊座（12月22日～1月19日） 自然体でOK。自分と世の中のペースのギャップに悩まされていた山羊座は、世の中のほうが少しばかり落ち着いてくるため、急いで適応しなくてもよい状態に。新しいツールを使いこなせないわけではなく、あなた自身が「少し違和感を感じる」ということだったのでしょう。その感覚が間違いではなかったと、いくつかの場面で立証されそうです。山羊座が先導し、猛烈な仕事ぶりを発揮してきたグループは、解散か休止のサイン。そのまま突進していくと事故が起こりやすいかもしれません。新たなリーダーを後輩世代から立てるか、プロジェクトそのものを吟味するか。 山羊座と相性のよい牡牛座、乙女座とのメンバーシップは、少し距離を置いたほうがベター。相手の方が休暇願いを出してくるかもしれません。心の底から「遊ぶ」ということが、実はあまり得意でない山羊座ですが、遊ぶのが義務になるくらいなら、何もしないのがベストです。お金をたくさん使うのも嫌いな山羊座。健康のメンテナンスには少しかけてもいいかもしれません。 今月の山羊座におすすめのラッキー・アルバム：グレナディア・ガーズ・バンドによる『星条旗よ永遠なれ〜スーザ：マーチ名曲集』 山羊座の2026年下半期の運勢 水瓶座（1月20日～2月18日） 少しばかり強引な「断捨離推奨月間」です。モノに関してもため込みすぎはマイナスに。美しいものをたくさん持っているのに、数が多すぎるためにゴミ溜めのようになっていないかチェックを。空間には癒されるべきであり、その空間からエネルギーを吸われるようでは本末転倒です。水瓶座の瓶は知恵を溜めこむための瓶なので、雑誌や紙の資料などは捨てるのに決意がいるかも。一度始めればスムーズに完了します。断捨離マスターの助けを借りるのもあり。 仕事面でも、シリアスな断捨離の局面が訪れていて、あなたの献身やエネルギーを受け取ってもらえない仕事場からは去りどき。現実面ではそうもいかないケースが多いはずですが、信頼できる人に相談するだけでも状況は軽くなってきます。「これだけは譲れない」といった仕事に一本化し、マルチな仕事スタイルはセーブしていくのもおすすめ。プライベートは花や植物と触れ合う楽しさを満喫して。 今月の水瓶座におすすめのラッキーアルバム：リュビモフが弾くケージ『ケージ：フォー・ウォールズ』 水瓶座の2026年下半期の運勢 魚座（2月19日～3月20日） 8月28日に魚座で起こっていた満月は、あなたにとって大きな流れの一区切りで、9月は新しい気分で清々しくスタートしていきます。他人と自分を比べず、自分だけの幸せを追求していきたい、という姿勢は揺るぎないものになっていきそう。組織に所属していてもフリーランスでも、魚座は基本的に自由なのです。 誰かとムキになって対立したり、白黒をはっきりつけようとするのもあなたのやり方ではないので、この時期は誰とも戦わず、競争心も見せずにニュートラルに振舞って。仕事上のパートナーは、きっちり几帳面タイプが意外にも好相性。乙女座とはいいコンビになるでしょう。細かいもめごとも相手が解決してくれます。 新しく知り合う相手には、最初からプライベートの事情などは明かさず、ざっくりビジネスライクに接したほうが◎。これまで秘密まで打ち明けて失敗したケースがあったら、それを繰り返さないことです。浪費傾向のある魚座は、ここで習慣を変えられそう。空しいことにはお金を使わないことです。 今月の魚座におすすめのラッキーアルバム：セリーヌ・モワネによる『ベゾッティ/ルクレール/リヒター:バロック・オーボエ協奏曲集』 魚座の2026年下半期の運勢 【2026年後半《総括》】2026年下半期は誰もが「主役」！

items.body: 会期：2026/07/02～2026/07/05 会場：一心寺 南会所［大阪府］ 公式サイト：https://hmp-theater.com/work/kanidenka/ リーディング公演は、「本公演のための試演会」「低予算でも可能な簡易版」と思われがちだ。だが、大がかりな舞台セットや音響、照明、衣装などの演出で色を付けられない分、「声に出して読む」という戯曲の本質が抽出され、戯曲自体の構造がクリアに浮かび上がる。とりわけ、リフレインのリズム感、アンサンブルによる音楽的リズムの増幅、居酒屋のメニューや街中の看板など「演劇の台詞として書かれたものではない言葉」を戯曲に取り込む手法が駆使されている場合、「リーディング」という形式の意義や魅力が際立つ。 リーディング公演『KANIDENKA』は、維新派を主宰した松本雄吉の没後10年を契機とし、大阪を拠点とする劇団、エイチエムピー・シアターカンパニーが企画した。構成・演出は、同カンパニーの俳優で、維新派に一時在籍していた髙安美帆。松本は1970年に「日本維新派」を結成し、1987年に「維新派」と改称した後、1991年の『少年街』にて「ヂャンヂャン☆オペラ」という独自のスタイルを確立した。劇団員自らが巨大な野外劇場を建設・解体し、5拍子や7拍子のリズムに乗せて大阪弁で語るのが特徴である。名称は、活動拠点の大阪にある、通天閣で知られる下町「新世界」にあるジャンジャン横丁から取られている。 1984年初演の『蟹殿下』は、初期の日本維新派時代から独自のスタイルを確立するまでの過渡期にある作品だが、原点といえる要素が多く詰まっている。例えば、「淡路島」「小豆島」「豊島」「直島」と羅列される島の名前が、瀬戸内海から九州南端へと抜け、奄美大島、沖縄島、宮古島、そしてパラオ、ミクロネシア連邦、マーシャル諸島など大日本帝国時代に委任統治領となった南洋諸島を含む島々へと続いていくシーンは、後の代表作『台湾の、灰色の牛が背のびをしたとき』（2010）を既に内包している。戯曲は『維新派・松本雄吉 1946～1970～2016』（‎リトルモア、2018）に収録。 「蟹殿下」と宛名が書かれた巨大な封筒が地面から出現して始まる『蟹殿下』には、明確なストーリーはない。ジャンジャン横丁に迷い込んだ蟹（＝酔っ払った放浪の男）が、「親愛なる路地の殿下へ……」と呼びかける女たちの声に誘われ、飲み屋街から路地を抜けて南港の海まで歩いていく旅が、さまざまな情景や言葉のコラージュとして描かれる。南港フェリーターミナル広場での初演時には、更地に碁盤の目の溝を掘り、その上に板と土をかぶせて再び更地に見えるようにした仮設劇場を建設。作中に頻出する「穴」「マンホール」のように出演者が地中から出入りし、クライマックスではクレーンに吊り下げた巨大な月が昇る演出がなされた。また、ト書きでの情景描写に加え、記録写真を見ると、ふんどし一丁の出演者が金粉ショーを披露するなど、ビジュアル要素の強い上演であったことがわかる。この戯曲を、ビジュアルに頼らずに、俳優の声によってどう立ち上げることができるか。 ［撮影：井上嘉和］ リーディング公演で強く感じたのは、演劇として都市の路上へ眼差しを向けること、そして異なるレンズの使用によって視野や解像度の違いが浮かび上がる点だ。本作では、鳥の目のように俯瞰する視線と、虫のように地べたを這う視線が同居する。「通天閣の向こうがわは？」「ジャンジャン横丁」「ジャンジャン横丁の向こうがわは？」「まちだ胃腸病院」「まちだ胃腸病院の向こうがわは？」「てんのじ村」と続く問答は、娯楽施設、学校、橋、変電所、貯木場と街中のランドマークを点と点でつなぎながら飛び越え、南港フェリー埠頭に着地する。そこから先に広がるのは、淡路島から瀬戸内海を越え、太平洋へと果てしなくつながる島の数々だ。一方、本作のキーワードのひとつが、「蟹」と「亀」という、海を生まれ故郷とし、地べたをのろのろと這う生き物だ。ジャンジャン横丁で酔っ払った男は、路地に迷い込んだ亀を見つけ、「かわいそうになあ、よーし、俺が連れて帰ったる、海まで連れて行ったる、まかしとけ、ジャンジャン横丁案内して、海まで連れて行ったる、（略）ちょっと酔うてはおるけどなあ、海まで行く道はよう知っとんのや」と掌に載せる。社会から「虫けら」のように踏み潰され、除け者にされる存在どうしの人情と、頼りなさや情けなさ。また、ト書きでは終盤、路地を放浪する男たちが体を寄せ合うと、頭の被り物が亀の甲羅に変容し、吹き上がる水しぶきのなか、ゆっくりと海へ向かって歩いていく。 また、路地の点描のシーンでは、「ビール大三八〇エン」「エビフライ三八〇エン」「冷ヤッコ一〇〇エン」といった壁のメニュー、「権利金保証金なし」のアパートの張り紙や街中の看板の文字が読み上げられる。「演劇の台詞」として書かれたものではないが、注文の際、声に出して読まれる言葉。酒や娯楽、宿を探し求めて路上を歩く人々に呼びかける看板の文字。街中には潜在的な演劇の台詞が膨大に存在している。松本の視線は、街を歩きながらそれらを収集し、コラージュする。再開発や観光地化でもう存在しない街並みを、断片的な言葉として収集・保存する、アーカイブとしての戯曲がここに立ち上がる。複数の道が交差する都市の路上はまた、直線的な一筋の道で物語化することへの抵抗ともなる。また、本作は、ヴァルター・ベンヤミンが『パサージュ論』で提示した、近代都市の消費空間をそぞろ歩く「遊歩者」のバリエーション（大阪の下町バージョン）ともいえるだろう。 ［撮影：井上嘉和］ 戯曲ではただの情報や文字の羅列だったものが、複数の声で読まれ、時にアンサンブルとして共鳴することで、立体的な音響として世界が実体的に立ち上がる。円環状に並ぶ俳優たちの間を、リフレインの台詞が順番に連なることで、言葉が渦を巻くようなループ構造が出現する。特に、クライマックスに配置された「スズメ啼ケ啼ケ、スズメ啼ケ啼ケ、千匹啼ケ万匹啼ケ、千匹啼ケ万匹啼ケ」「セミ啼ケ啼ケ、セミ啼ケ啼ケ、千匹啼ケ万匹啼ケ、千匹啼ケ万匹啼ケ」「カモメ啼ケ啼ケ、カモメ啼ケ啼ケ、千匹啼ケ万匹啼ケ、千匹啼ケ万匹啼ケ」というリフレインは、複数人で同じリズムを刻んで読むことで、身体運動を伴った集団的な祝祭へと高揚していく。海へ向かう行進から、ビートに乗るように体を揺らす集団へ。マラソンランナーや暴走族といった都市の通過者がそこに交差する。「夜明ケマデ、アト何時間？ ドウゾ」「夜明ケマデ、アト三〇分、ドウゾ」、「夜明ケマデ、アト何分？ ドウゾ」「夜明ケマデ、アト三分、ドウゾ」、「夜明ケマデ、アト何分？ ドウゾ」「夜明ケマデ、アト五〇秒、ドウゾ」という通信兵たちが執拗に繰り返すリフレインは、終幕までの時間、「遊び」の時間の終わりを告げるカウントダウンでもある。 ［撮影：井上嘉和］ 一方、本作では、ジェンダーの対称性が（「男たち」「女たち」という集団性と匿名化によっても）極めて明瞭に引かれている構造も浮かび上がる。男たちは、野良犬のように路地を放浪するが、女たちは、「赤いカフェ」「青いカフェ」「桃色のカフェ」と色とりどりのネオンで名指された場所（風俗街）に固定されて動けない。また、「青いカフェの女」は、「あなた、ゲイジュツはもうやめてください」と繰り返し懇願する。「自分を慕って待ち続ける女を振り切ってこそ、男は世俗と隔絶した芸術家になれる」という特権的な芸術家像がここに露呈する。さらには、「女」は芸術家にはなれず、「男＝孤独にさすらう芸術家」をいつまでも待ち続け、優しく抱きしめてくれる存在として描写するジェンダー観も明らかだ。 ビジュアルの要素が強い舞台だからこそ、俳優の声によって戯曲の構造に解像度を上げて迫ることができる。リーディング公演の可能性を提示してくれる機会だった。 鑑賞日：2026/07/05（日） 関連レビュー VISIONEN -ドイツ同時代演劇リーディング・シリーズVol. 9 『HOMOHALAL（ホモハラル）』｜高嶋慈：artscapeレビュー（2019年12月15日号） 松本雄吉 追悼特集｜高嶋慈：artscapeレビュー（2016年12月15日号）

items.excerpt: 大阪大学 中之島センターにて、「Art for Well-being」プロジェクトの一環として、ハッカソン「表現×ケア×テクノロジー 現場ではじめるための実践ワークショップ」が開催されます。 本イベントは、心身のケアの選択肢や重度の障害のある人の表現活動の支援として、体験しながら学ぶワークショップです。福祉や医療の現場で活動している人や、技術者やアーティスト、デザイナー、研究者、コーディネーターなどが集まり、チームになってアイデア出し、会場で準備した道具を組み合わせて発表する2日間のプログラムとなっています。 特別な技術や知識は不要です。申込詳細は下記および、公式サイトをご覧ください。 ＜ハッカソンとは？＞ おもにITエンジニアリングなどの世界で使われる言葉で、Hack（ハック）＆Marathon（マラソン）を組み合わせた造語です。さまざまな専門性や関心を持つ人たちが集まり、決められた時間と空間で成果を出します。完璧な答えや作品をつくるのが目的ではなく、そこから新しい発想や行動を生みだすためのワークショップです。 開催プログラム 【1日目】「知る、触れる、考える」 日時｜2026/09

items.body: August 14 - 16, 2026, Peitz, Germany Up a creaky set of wooden stairs to the lofts of the 1810 Huettenwerk of the historic Ironworks and Fishery Museum of Peitz, an imposing building full of old heavy tools for the iron foundry and fishing works in the surrounding carp ponds, is an exhibition on Free Jazz in the German Democratic Republic (former East Germany). It’s a traveling show, having accompanied Jazzwerkstatt concerts and festivals over the years. The first time I encountered it, at a Globe Unity Orchestra concert in Potsdam in 2014, it prompted me to dig for all of the Amiga Jazz records that I could find, leading to likely the most complete collection of East German jazz in New Jersey. Every year for the past ten years or so that I’ve been to the festival, I find myself drawn to the exhibition, like a pilgrim to worship. Each station of the exhibit offers a glimpse into this well documented but still mythical past, with a final station showcasing the Peitz Festival. Created in 1973 by two young free-thinking music fans, Uli Blobel and Peter “Jimi” Metag, both from the small East German town of Peitz, the festival drew other like minded youth to hear both East German musicians like Ernst-Ludwig Petrowsky and Conny Bauer as well as West German musicians like Alexander von Schlippenbach and other musicians from the other side of the Iron Curtain such as Barry Guy and Wadada Leo Smith. The names are many and the history can be read in the “Woodstock am Karpfenteich’ books as well as experienced here , and the story is a good one. Lasting until shut down by the government in 1982 and restarted by Blobel in 2011 under much different conditions, the Jazzwerkstatt Peitz festival of 2026 still draws some of those who trekked by train and Trabi to the original, but is also working to draw in a new audience whose connection to the past is being built by heading to upper floors via creaky wooden stairs. Starting in 2024, Marie Blobel, the daughter of Uli Blobel, took over. Some of the changes Marie Blobel made included moving the festival from the center of Peitz to the grounds of the fishing museum amidst the carp ponds and injecting a festive flair into the weekend long event. With a packed schedule of concerts and a two kilometer hike to the Doener restaurant, festival goers are oriented to the wurst stand, the home cooked vegetarian dishes at the beer tent and the biergarten around the corner. Kids have the chance to make their own music with an imaginative looping station and everyone can climb aboard the “Karpfenbummler,” an electric miniature train that will take you in style from the festival to town to the train station. Coming into its own it the new form, Jazzwerkstatt Peitz was awarded the Deutsche Jazzpreis this past year. -- Gebhard Ullman’s Hemisphere 4 PLUS (biergarten stage) The concerts began on Friday evening with the folk-meets-modern-jazz sounds of Trio Ivoire . In the trio's music, Hans Lüdemann ’s piano and electronics and Christian Thomé 's percussion and electronics are met with the organic tones of Aly Keïta ’s balafon, an African instrument described as a “ a gourd-resonated xylophone .” The music is upbeat and highly syncopated and thus quickly had some of the at-capacity audience on their feet swaying to their rhythms. As soon as the set ended, the audience began shuffling off, around the museum and cycler hostel (the Gurkenradweg - yes, the Pickle Bikepath - passes by the festival grounds), to a biergarten, where a stage has been set up under a lush copse of trees. Woodwindist Gebhard Ullman ’s newest formation, Hemisphere 4 PLUS , featuring a mix of his current electric and acoustic groups, began with a chamber-jazz like combination of Anna Viechtl ’s harp and Taiko Saito’s vibraphone. Disrupted by a crash of percussion, the group tumbled into a pulsating groove. Describing the music as “sculptures,” Ullmann led the group through an alluring mix of the delicate (add Silke Lange accordion to the chamber jazz components), hard-hitting (with Eric Schaefer on drums and Oliver Potratz on bass) and other-worldly ( Liz Kosack ’s keyboard and synthesizer). OM (main stage) A short shuffle back to the main stage where OM , the legendary avant-jazz-rock group, were ready to go. The original group members, saxophonist Urs Leimgruber , guitarist Christy Doran and bassist Bobby Burri were joined by drummer’s Gerry Hemingway and Tony Buck who have replaced the late Fredy Studer, as they did on the recent Intakt release Suedpol . After a short freely improvised intro from Leimgruber, a blast of rock energy from Doran gave root to a swirling squall of tones and the music slowly evolved into a groove led by the two percussionists. Moments of electric Miles colored the rich panoply of sound which ranged from deeply experimental to outright rock. An excellent set. Closing out the main stage for the evening was the quartet Selvhenter from Copenhagen. Saxophonist Sonja LaBianca and trombonist Maria Bertel and drummers Anja Jacobsen and Jaleh Negari crafted a dark, throbbing techno-jazz designed to get festival goers on their feet. It was quite late by the time the quartet’s final notes faded, but the show wasn’t over … yet, as drummer Willi Kellers and organizer Wolfgang ‘Assi’ Gloede were hosting a jam session in the cozy workshop building behind the main stage. Amongst painted fish sculptures and some serious looking tools, saxophonist Lotte Anker , keyboardist Liz Kosack and bassist Reza Askari joined Kellers in free-jazz improvisation that began with electronic percolations and slowly crescendoing notes that eventually balled into an exciting and thorny tumbleweed of sound. Following the opener, Gloede curated combinations of professional and hobbyist musicians who improvised into the wee hours. -- Wanja Slavin (sitting far right) (church) Saturday’s full schedule began in the town church where saxophonist and festival Improviser-in-Residence Wanja Slavin , last year’s winner of the Brandenburg Jazzpreis - an award developed by Jazzwerkstatt and the state of Brandenburg - debuted a new composition with a band comprised of Peter Evans on trumpet, Leonard Huhn on bass clarinet, Almut Kühne with vocals and Kaja Draksler on piano. The rich 45-minute piece moved seamlessly between moods and approaches as darker moments were balanced by more hopeful passages. Repetitive arpeggios and prominent electronics formed a consistent tonal base accentuated by the dissonant church organ and several outstanding solos. A short while later back at the festival grounds, percussionist and singer Mariá Portugal’s EROSÃO septet took the stage in the rapidly heating up early afternoon. The music began with a brass fanfare as the group walked-on the stage and transitioned to Portugal singing over polyrhythmic accompaniment. Concentrated on a repertoire of songs that drew heavily on her Brazilian background, Portugal’s vocals took center stage, while the high-powered group of saxophonists Lotte Anker and Angelika Niescier , trombonists Matthias Müller and Moritz Wesp , tubist Carl Ludwig Hübsch and bassist Reza Askari provided solid support. Afterwards in the Huettenwerk building, the duo of Mohammad Mostafa Heydarian and Valentin Portron , performing on the traditional Iranian tanbur and bendir - a stringed instrument and hand drum - continued the expansion of the festival’s musical purview. Impro-Concert: Tony Buck, Matthias Mueller, Taito Saito (workshop) Two improvisation sessions, tucked away in the workshop building, injected a bit of the unexpected into the afternoon. The first introduced the British woodwindist Tamar Osborn with the American bassist Nick Dunston and drummer Gerry Hemingway . This first meeting proved fruitful. Clicking quickly, Osborn leaned into the deeper registers of her baritone sax, while Hemingway contributed a lithe, but full, pulse and Dunston provided a melodically swinging bridge between the two. The later improvisation session joined three Berlin based improvisors who have been in each other’s orbits but never played together before. Vibraphonist Taiko Saito , trombonist Matthias Müller and drummer Tony Buck played a set ranging from contemplative to combustive. Aki Takase, Robert Landfermann, Christian Lillinger. (c) Cristina Marx/Photomusix The mid-afternoon offered both unforgiving sun and an excellent set from pianist Aki Takase who was performing her upbeat, complex, and often humor-laced music with drummer Christian Lillinger and bassist Robert Landfermann on the main stage. The trio’s music is impressive, Lillinger, with his agitated, driving approach is a perfect rhythmic partner for Takase’s own intensity, and Landfermann’s rhythmic and melodic playing adds a nicely fitting layer. Nearing the end of the set, a dramatic moment ensured when Takase suddenly collapsed from the heat. Fortunately, it was reported that the pianist was already on the move to the next concert in Austria that evening. Darius Jones & Otomo Yoshihide Quartet. (c) Cristina Marx/Photomusix A little later the shows were back in the biergarten, where the trees provided some relief from the 100 degree heat, and the Czech quartet Edemit added a jolt of avant-rock to the day while Neiscer and Portugal picked up in a duo form the earlier set. As the day began to cool, the action moved back on the main stage where Darius Jones and Otomo Yoshihide (alto saxophone and guitar, respectively) augmented by bassist Nick Dunston and drummers Gerald Cleaver and Yasuhiro Yoshigaki provided an electric set. Following a rousing Coltrane-like introduction, the rhythm section gave Jones a rumbling foundation for his soaring melody to which Yoshihide responded with a feedback-laden solo, pushing the music to an early peak. The music ebbed and flowed, from dark atmospheric wanderings to high-energy free-jazz explosions over pulsating rhythms. Afterwards, the UK-based Ill Considered featuring Tamar Osborn ( Idris Rahman on saxophone, Liran Donin on bass, Emre Ramazanoglu on drums and Osborn with various woodwinds) closed out the night with a set heavy on beats and Middle Eastern-tinged scales. The set ended with about half the remaining audience dancing in front of the stage. -- Perhaps in normal times, it would have been a disappointment but after the previous day’s oven-like disposition, the cool, rain-soaked grey morning greeting festival goers on Sunday was welcome. A church service in the Huettenwerk started the day for the faithful while out on the festival yard, the others were huddling under the drink stand tents sipping coffee while the bratwurst man started up his grill. First musical act, Richard Koch’s Ray of Light was the only one to be seen under the steadily raining sky. They began with the trumpeter playing a regal anthem and launching into a cheery, melodic tune filled with the folkish sounds of Fabiana Striffler ’s violin and Valentin Butt ’s accordion along with the rhythm support of Andreas Lang ’s bass and Nora Thiele ’s frame drums. The “gute laune” (good mood) music with its blend of up-tempo jazz, classical and folk elements provided a lighthearted start to another long day of music. Their timing was perfect too, as Ray of Light reached the end of their set, the first beams of sun reached the festival grounds. Have You Ever Been Experienced. (c) Cristina Marx/Photomusix The opening set was followed by Brandenburg Jazzpreis. Prize winner, guitarist Andreas Willers , who was to present his Hendrix inspired group Have You Ever Been Experienced , featuring a top-notch group of Berlin based musicians: Amy Green on vocals, Rieko Okuda on piano, Jan Roder on bass and Christian Marien on drums, was unfortunately too ill to attend. Despite this, the group, still gave a rousing performance, taking well-worn Hendrix themes and spinning them anew. Okuda took over the guitar solos with a distorted synthesizer, while Roder and Marien made sure the foundations were securely fortified. Most revelatory were Green’s vocals, which retained enough of the melody for song-recognition and enough improvisational liberty to free them from nostalgic interpretation -- for example, an updated interpretation of Allen Ginsberg’s Howl set to a free-jazz take of ‘If 6 was 9.’ The final two sets of the festival moved back into town to the church. The first was the Polish duo of vocalist Maniucha Bikont and bassist Ksawery Wójciński performing a set of haunting folksongs. Discovered through Bikont’s musicology research, the songs came from a disappearing tribe in the Ukraine, with themes that touched on the universal: suffering, responsibility and expecting better manners from the dead. Performed solely with voice and bass, the music filled the church mesmerizingly. Konradism. (c) Cristina Marx/Photomusix The closing set to the festival may have also been one of the most anticipated. Connecting the festival’s eras, trombonist and archetype of the original Peitz festival and East German free-jazz in general, trombonist Conny Bauer presented the large group Konradisms with an extended composition of “chamber big-band” that mixed generous improvisation and dramatic riffs. Joining Bauer was a cross section of a younger generation of German-based musicians: Nils Wogram on trombone, Maxine Troglauer also on bass trombone, Gerhard Gschlössl on tuba, Claudio Puntin on bass clarinet, Maria Reich on violin, Emily Wittbrodt on cello, Matthias Bauer on bass, Dag Magnus Narvesen on drums and Rieko Okuda on piano. Often breaking into small combos - trombone and piano, tuba and violin - the solos would grow intense and eventually congeal around common themes. A stand out was Puntin whose bass clarinet playing ranged from the sound of a flute to deep, woody resonance. After an intense two and half days of music, the two last concerts were a satisfying and full-circle-moment ending to the festival. Overall, one could sense a tilt towards the new - nights that ended with experimental but danceable music, a series of risky but successful workshop concerts with musicians meeting for the first time, an infusion of world-music elements, and a loosening, but not denying, deference to the past, showing a way forward. More about the Peitz festival: Review of the 50th Anniversary Peitz Festival Review of the Jazzwerkstatt Peitz Boxset Jazzwerkstatt Peitz website . Email This BlogThis! Share to X Share to Facebook

items.body: Label: True Sound Recordings, 2026 Personnel - Jason Kao Hwang: violin; Ken Filiano: bass; Andrew Drury: drums, percussion. American violinist Jason Kao Hwang, a mainstay of New York’s downtown avant-garde scene, reunites with his highly adaptable Human Rites Trio, featuring bassist Ken Filiano and drummer/percussionist Andrew Drury, for a new album. Second Life comprises four extended Hwang compositions delineated by rich ebbing and flowing exchanges and constantly shifting passages, enriched by unconventional melodic constructions and perceptible rhythmic ripples. “ Galaxies Twist Under Before It ” initially unfolds over a 12-beat bass groove that mutates into a 4/4 funk-rock scenario. Hwang’s screaming solo explores several registers of the violin through euphoric improvisational flurries, supported by Drury’s sagacious fills. The drummer has ample space to expand his chops, and the trio reaches a crescendo through deliberate deconstructions. A quieter passage of plucked violin and understated drumming welcomes Filiano’s solo. After the theme returns, the trio enters a reflective state marked by lachrymose violin, tactful arco work, and colorful cymbal splashes. “ What to Keep, What to Let Go ” begins as a ballad, but its gradual expansions and contractions lead into an improvised scenario packed with energy. There are great moments to savor during Hwang’s improvisation, but one cannot overlook the outstanding work of the rhythm section, which introduces radical shifts while toggling between marching postures and swinging delirium. Filiano’s excellent arco technique and deep, resonant sound are are something to be reckoned with. “ Ricochet ” offers motif-inflected tapestries, funk grooves, and avant-chamber passages centered on improvisation. Drury lays down a skillfully articulated and harmonious percussive flow here. Honest expressionism is integral to the trio’s style, with each creative idea pushed into free and open territory. Favorite Tracks: 01 - Galaxies Twist Under Before It ► 04 - Ricochet
